h: Teshuvah Reveals the Beauty Hidden in Every Jewish Soul

p: "Are you not like the children of the Kushites to Me, etc."
And I heard from our holy Rebbe,
may the memory of the righteous and holy be a blessing,
of the outcry of the young
over the matter of blemishing the bris.
And we find in the Gemara (Berachos 20a)
who would sit at the gates of immersion,
and he remained from "the beautiful ones of Yerushalayim"
in the holiness of the bris;
for he said: "I do not fear the evil eye,
I come from the seed of Yosef"
alluding to the holiness of the bris,
as it says (in the Gemara, Berachos there):
to feed on what is not its own
the evil eye will not rule over it."
one who blemishes the holiness of the bris
וּכְעֵין שֶׁמָּצִינוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לו)
similar to what we find in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 36):
for this was a blemish of the bris,
since relations had been forbidden to them.
וְאׇמְנָם בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל כָּתַב (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים א, ו)
However, regarding Yisrael it writes (Shir HaShirim 1:6):
"Do not look at me that I am swarthy,
for the sun has tanned me";
for in truth all of Yisrael
and it is only because of the leaven in the dough
and through the washing of teshuvah
וְזֶה שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר אַחַר זֶה (עָמוֹס ט, ט)
And this is what it says after this (Amos 9:9):
"And I will shake among all the nations
as one shakes with a sieve,
and not a pebble shall fall to the ground, etc."
That is, the root of the exiles
which is an offshoot of bloodshed,
as they said in the Gemara (Niddah 13a)
"Who inflame yourselves among the terebinths, etc.";
that he was sentenced to exile,
because he was a shedder of blood.
And it says in the writings of the Arizal, of blessed memory,
that the exile in Egypt was
to rectify the corruption of Adam HaRishon
in the one hundred thirty years
and the souls that were in Egypt
of the generation of the Flood;
and in Egypt they rectified the blemish
in that they were fenced off from forbidden unions;
וּכִדְאִיתָא בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (שִׁיר הַשִּׁירִים רַבָּה ד, יב)
as it says in the Midrash (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:12):
and all the males were fenced off in his merit."
of not being unrestrained in forbidden unions
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (וַיִּקְרָא רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה לב)
as they said in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah 32).
And our Sages, of blessed memory, said
"'Like the practice of the land of Egypt, etc.,
and like the practice of the land of Canaan, etc.,
this tells that the practices of the Egyptians
were the most corrupt of all the nations,
was the most corrupt of all."
And specifically to such a place
to extract from there the sparks of holiness;
that is, as is written in the holy Zohar
except that which comes out of darkness."
And this is what it says:
"And I will shake among all the nations, etc.,
and not a pebble shall fall to the ground";
all the souls of Yisrael will be refined,
And this is alluded to in the Gemara (Taanis 20b),
in the episode of Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon:
"There chanced upon him a certain man
Peace be upon you, Rabbi, etc.
He said to him: Empty one!
How ugly is that man, etc.
Go and say to the Craftsman Who made me:
How ugly is this vessel that You made."
and he intended it for the good,
so that he would not make a habit of the matter.
That is, Rabbi Elazar the son of Rabbi Shimon,
because he had learned much Torah
that is, he was holy in this matter,
by one who stumbled in this matter,
And Eliyahu, the angel of the bris,
on account of which all Yisrael are called
"Once he is circumcised he is called a tzaddik"
it was hard in his eyes
that Rabbi Elazar was repelled by
even the soul that stumbled in this matter;
the souls of Yisrael are righteous,
and "our will is to do Your will;
only the leaven in the dough prevents us"
and through teshuvah everything is healed,
and "not a pebble shall fall to the ground,"
and the light will increase even more
as a man ugly with blackness,
which comes from blemishing the bris;
וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר הָיָה מְמָאֵס אוֹתוֹ לְגַמְרֵי
and Rabbi Elazar was utterly repelled by him
and did not return his greeting;
"Go say to the Craftsman Who made me:
How ugly is this vessel that You made";
so that the light come from within the darkness.
וּכְמוֹ כֵן מָצִינוּ בַּגְּמָרָא (נְדָרִים נ, ב)
And likewise we find in the Gemara (Nedarim 50b)
"In what does your father put wine, etc.?"
put it in vessels of silver and gold";
they would be even more learned."
to the light that comes out of darkness;
and this is alluded to in what she said to him:
and to this he answered her
and in vessels of silver it spoils;
for His will, may He be blessed, is
אֶלָּא הַהִיא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא וְכוּ׳
except that which comes out of darkness," etc.
belongs to the parsha "You shall be holy,"
for our Sages, of blessed memory, said:
"On that day I will raise up
the fallen booth of Dovid, etc.,
and I will return the captivity
Mashiach will be the individual who repents,
for whose sake the whole world is forgiven
And certainly it would not avail
the repentance of an individual for the whole world;
that he will bring a thought of teshuvah
and all will return in teshuvah;
וְשַׁבְתִּי אֶת שְׁבוּת עַמִּי יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳
"and I will return the captivity of My people Yisrael, etc."
"And I will plant them on their land,
and they shall no longer be uprooted
for the holiness of Eretz Yisrael
is that it does not tolerate this blemish,
"And the land vomited out its inhabitants, etc.";
"they shall no longer be uprooted from upon their land."
And this passage is always read
for it says in Sefer Yetzirah:
"He made the letter vav king over thought, etc.,
for all the days of the Counting
as the Arizal, of blessed memory, writes;
and mainly in the month of Iyar,
which was created with the letter vav, over thought.
one vav is the letter of truth,
the vav of the spelled-out letter
And all the days of the Counting
for the blemish of the bris,
as it says in the Midrash (this parsha):
"One who used to learn one page
and the Torah is a cure
for the covenant of the flesh
and for the covenant of the tongue,
"A healing tongue is a tree of life";
and our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Arachin 15b):
"'Tree of life' means nothing but Torah,
דִּכְתִיב (מִשְׁלֵי ג, יח) עֵץ חַיִּים הוּא וְגוֹ׳
as it is written (Mishlei 3:18), 'It is a tree of life, etc.'";
and it is a cure for the covenant of the tongue.
which also alludes to the covenant of the flesh,
"And My covenant shall be in your flesh."
that the mitzvah "You shall be holy"
"sanctify yourself in what is permitted to you"
in all matters of bodily pleasure,
which is the root of the serpent,
who brought in that a person should feel
is to rectify the entire root of the blemish.
